newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate bounces up to 10.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate bounces up to 10.8 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate bounced back up to 10.8 percent on Thursday from 9.6 percent despite good supply as more borrowers sought term funds.
Overall demand on the local money market shrank to 17 million kuna, against more than three times that in supply.
But dealers said some lenders still charged relatively high rates for term loans, with one-month bank borrowings fetching 15.0 percent.
Call money was flat at 9.0 percent and insurers' funds at 8.0 percent.
As a period of good liquidity continued, only 0.5 million kuna were traded at Wednesday's overnight session.
The central bank's kuna midrates were calculated firmer at 5.3804 to the dollar and 3.5667 to the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
